chunks: Sama'ah asked him about a woman in ihram wearing silk, so he said:
It is not proper for her to wear pure silk with no mixture in it.
As for khazz and decorative trimming in the garment, there is no harm in her wearing it while she is in ihram.
If a man passes by her, she should conceal herself from him with her garment, and she should not shade herself from the sun with her hand.
And she may wear khazz. Indeed, they will say that there is silk in khazz, but what is disliked is solid, undifferentiated silk.

key_terms.الْخَزُّ: khazz, a mixed fabric that includes silk
key_terms.الْعَلَمُ: decorative marking or trim on a garment
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمَةِ: a woman in the state of ihram
key_terms.حَرِيرًا مَحْضًا: pure silk with no other material mixed into it

ai.seo_question: Can a woman in ihram wear silk or silk-blended clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings for a woman in ihram regarding clothing. It prohibits pure silk, permits khazz and garment decoration containing silk, and mentions how she should conceal herself from men during ihram.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2635 - Sama'ah asked Imam (as) about a woman in Ihram wearing silk.
Imam (as) said: "It is not proper for her to wear pure silk without any mixture.
However, there is no harm if she wears khazz (a silk-blended fabric) or a garment with embroidery while she is in Ihram.
If a man passes by her, she should cover herself with her garment but not use her hand to shield herself from the sun.
She may wear khazz, although people may say that khazz contains silk. What is disliked is pure silk."
